reflection.review:
10 of 10 planned draft attempts implemented, prechecked, and scored (one
scored validator run each, serial, single-threaded). 1 of 10 passed the
GOAL.md bar: attempt-004 (greedy cost-function portfolio + budget-bug-fixed
TreeSA ramp) achieved the **speed win** — baseline tc within 0.3 on every
dev instance at T/4 budget — and then passed the **holdout** adjudication
(speed_win=true, generalization_guard=true, all 15 instance×budget pairs
valid, including reg3_300, larger than any dev graph). Scores (mean Δtc,
higher better; baseline candidate reference −0.23):

- 001 subtree-shift SA: −0.44 (reg3_250 sc-cap fails at T/4, T/16)
- 002 wall-clock cooling: −0.15 (reg3_250 sc-cap fails at T/4, T/16)
- 003 Boltzmann greedy seeds: −0.44 (same reg3_250 small-budget failure)
- 004 cost-fn portfolio + fixed ramp: **−0.11, speed_win, PASS dev+holdout**
- 005 min-cut builder: −0.81 (reg3_250 fails at all three budgets)
- 006 order-then-tree DP: −0.36 (reg3_250 fails at T/16 only)
- 007 elimination-order SA: −2.40 (11 non-pass incl. grid_4x4, reg3_50)
- 008 basin hopping: −0.55 (reg3_250 sc-cap at all budgets)
- 009 beam search: −1.54 (7 non-pass; reg3_100/250 quality + sc)
- 010 min-fill line graph: −0.44 (reg3_250 small-budget failures)

Budget state: 10/10 attempts used this authorization; authorized_rounds now
0. Distance to bar: bar MET (speed path). Holdout query budget: 1/1 spent
this cycle (on 004, passed). No protocol overrides recorded.
reflection.evidence:
- Bar met by 004: dev speed_win + holdout speed_win with generalization
  guard, zero errors (reports in `.worktrees/attempt-004/report*.json`).
- Baseline budgets contain ~4× slack (004, confirmed on holdout).
- reg3 expanders defeat constructive methods (005/007/009 refuted) —
  blacklist: recursive bisection, elimination-order SA with
  smallest-intermediate decode, beam search without sc-awareness.
- Coarse SA moves (subtree-shift, basin-hop perturbation) beat baseline
  TreeSA by 3–6 tc on reg3_250 at full budget (001, 008) — promoted
  direction, blocked only by sc handling.
- sc-cap at small budgets is the systematic killer (5 attempts) — root
  cause identified in TreeSA's soft sc_target=20 objective.
- Holdout: 1 query spent (004, passed). Dev-overfit risk for 004 is low —
  its mechanism (schedule hygiene) is instance-agnostic and replicated on
  unseen sizes.
reflection.literature:
The 004 result matches the anytime-protocol point in Gray–Kourtis
[gray_2020_hyper] (optimizers should be compared as best-so-far curves, and
default budgets are rarely on the knee of the curve); no paper in
`.knowledge/` claims the specific "TreeSA defaults overshoot 4×" schedule
result for OMEinsumContractionOrders-style TreeSA, so the claim appears
novel at the engineering-note level, not the algorithmic level. The
001/008 reg3_250 gains are consistent with the subtree-transfer results of
[anon_2025_optimizing]; a quality-win write-up would need a head-to-head
with cotengra's SA mode (pinned, not yet run — see CATALOG.md). Shelved
insights: none to promote (all six were Selected).

lessons.observation: 004 passed the speed bar with baseline algorithm + scheduling hygiene; every novel draft scored below it
lessons.root_cause: baseline TreeSA defaults overshoot: converged tc is reached in <= T/4 on all dev families, so measured budgets contain ~4x slack that only schedule hygiene can harvest
lessons.evidence: 004 per-instance table (T/4 tc == full-budget baseline on 8/9 graphs); 006 LOG (budget-bug fixes moved score more than its DP); holdout replication on unseen sizes
lessons.implication: honest claim: TreeSA-class quality at 4x less optimizer time; the +1.0 quality bar remains the open research target

lessons.observation: five SA-family attempts failed only on reg3_250 at reduced budgets, almost always via the sc-cap guard (sc 34-36 vs cap 35)
lessons.root_cause: TreeSA's soft sc_target=20/weight-1 objective exerts no pressure near sc 33-36, so short anneals emit whatever sc the trajectory has; attempts inherited this objective
lessons.evidence: identical failure signature across 001/002/003/008/010; 008 LOG: sc-floor tracking halved but did not eliminate violations
lessons.implication: treat sc as a hard constraint (reject/penalize above baseline_sc+2) in any future search objective

lessons.observation: all constructive drafts (005 min-cut, 007 elimination-order, 009 beam) matched TreeSA on structured graphs but lost 4-17 tc on reg3, worsening with size
lessons.root_cause: reg3 graphs are expanders: no balanced separators, no low-width monotone construction; only iterative refinement over full trees finds their low-width structure
lessons.evidence: 005 reg3_250 tc 59 vs 47; 007 plateau 64 vs 47 at 8s; 009 66-73 vs 47 with sc blow-ups
lessons.implication: blacklist pure constructive methods on expander-dominated suites; use at most as seeds

lessons.observation: 001 and 008 beat baseline by 3-6 tc on reg3_250 at full budget yet scored negative overall
lessons.root_cause: their wins were erased by the sc-cap lesson above plus equal weighting of small-budget pairs in the mean
lessons.evidence: 001 LOG (+4.8 at T on reg3_250); 008 LOG (tc 41-44 when sc permits); validator errors confined to sc entries
lessons.implication: quality-win path plausibly reachable: coarse-move refinement + hard sc constraint + 004's schedule — top-ranked next-cycle candidate

blacklist_new: recursive balanced bisection on random-regular (expander) instances — no balanced separators (005)

beam search without sc-awareness on expanders — state diversity insufficient, sc blow-ups (009)
